claims.claim: Human mitochondrial DNA is a circular genome carrying 37 genes
claims.definition: The human mitochondrial genome (mtDNA) is a closed circular double-stranded molecule of about 16,569 base pairs encoding 37 genes: 13 proteins, 22 transfer RNAs and 2 ribosomal RNAs. It is separate from the nuclear genome.
claims.authoritative_source: NCBI Books, 'Mitochondrial DNA' (Genes and Disease); Anderson et al., Nature 1981 (complete mtDNA sequence)
sources: NCBI Genes and Disease: Mitochondrial DNA

claims.claim: Mitochondria descend from a bacterium engulfed roughly 1.5 billion years ago (endosymbiosis)
claims.definition: The endosymbiotic theory holds that mitochondria derive from an alpha-proteobacterium taken up by an ancestral eukaryotic/archaeal host cell, with an established-or-derived age on the order of 1.4-2 billion years; 'about 1.5 billion years' is the commonly cited order of magnitude.
claims.authoritative_source: Lane & Martin, Nature 2010 (origin of mitochondria); Gray, Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology 2012
claims.notes: Age has uncertainty of a few hundred million years; narration uses the common order-of-magnitude figure.

claims.claim: Mitochondria keep a double membrane, their own ribosomes and their own DNA — bacterial heritage
claims.definition: Ultrastructure: an outer membrane plus an inner membrane folded into cristae; mitochondria contain 70S-type ribosomes and their own circular genome, all traits consistent with their bacterial ancestry.
claims.authoritative_source: Alberts et al., 'Molecular Biology of the Cell' (mitochondria chapter)
sources: Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell

claims.claim: Mitochondrial DNA is inherited almost exclusively through the mother
claims.definition: The egg contributes the vast majority of the zygote's mitochondria; paternal mtDNA is typically eliminated after fertilization, so mtDNA traces the maternal line. Rare paternal leakage exists but is exceptional.
claims.authoritative_source: NCBI Books, 'Mitochondrial DNA' (maternal inheritance); Luo et al., PNAS 2018 (paternal leakage rarity)
sources: NCBI Genes and Disease: Mitochondrial DNA
